_readme: Copy to config.json before running. config.json is gitignored because it carries a live account index; this file is committed and must never have one written into it. NO KEY GOES IN EITHER FILE -- the signer reads LIGHTER_API_KEY from the environment and nothing else does.
_lighterNote: accountIndex is a PLACEHOLDER until the operator sets it. It is a public number: anyone can read the account at api.rh.lighter.xyz/api/v1/account?by=index&value=<index>, which is exactly what the site links to so a viewer can check the fly's positions without trusting the page. apiKeyIndex 0-3 are reserved by Lighter for its own desktop and mobile interfaces, so a bot uses 4 or above. The api key is a LIGHTER-NATIVE key, not an EVM key, and is registered once against the account.

lighter._chainIdNote: TWO DIFFERENT CHAIN IDS AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. 4663 is Robinhood Chain, the L1 where the ZkLighter deposit contract lives -- keeper/harvest.js uses that one. 466324 is Lighter's own L2 behind api.rh.lighter.xyz, and EVERYTHING SIGNED FOR THE EXCHANGE uses it. Signing with 4663 verifies against the wrong domain and returns `21120 invalid signature` -- identical to a wrong key, an empty slot or a malformed order, which is what made it cost three live attempts to find.
lighter._exchangeLeverageNote: WHAT IS PUSHED TO THE EXCHANGE, and it is NOT the same number as trade.exposure.leverage. Cross margin liquidates on MAINTENANCE margin, which is a function of NOTIONAL -- so the account's leverage setting does not move a position's liquidation price at all. It only decides how much INITIAL margin each position locks. Setting the exchange high and sizing lower is therefore free headroom: at exchange 10x with sizing 5x, a full ten-slot book locks half the margin it would at exchange 5x, and is liquidated at exactly the same -14.1%. The sizing number is the one that decides risk; this one decides capital efficiency. Raising THIS is safe. Raising trade.exposure.leverage is not, and the note there says why.

_tradeNote: armed is the config seatbelt and --broadcast is the command-line one, and BOTH are required before anything is sent. maxNotionalUsd is a third, enforced inside the signing process itself, so a bug in the sizing cannot spend more than the operator armed whatever the keeper believes. Leave armed false until a full dry cycle has produced orders you agree with.

exposure._maxFractionNote: THE OPERATOR'S RISK BUDGET -- the only number in the product that is a policy rather than a measurement. At 1.0 a fully convinced, fully aroused fly puts one equity of NOTIONAL into one market, which at 10x leverage is one slot of margin out of ten. It was 0.25, then 0.5 to clear Lighter's $10 order floor on a $76 account; the slot arithmetic now does that job, so this is back to being a pure ceiling. The fly still moves inside it: conviction times appetite (octopamine against serotonin) decides how much of the allowance it actually takes.
exposure._scaleNote: THE THREE LIMITS THAT ONLY MATTER WITH REAL MONEY, each measured rather than guessed. maxFraction is PER MARKET; maxTotalFraction caps the SUM, because the fly picks a different market most passes and never revisits the last one -- without it a simulated day on $5,000 reached 1.96x equity across eleven markets, which is leverage nobody asked for. deadbandFraction stops the reconciler chasing conviction noise: re-targeting every 44%-100% swing turned over 133x the account in that same day, about $331/day of slippage on $5,000. staleAfterMinutes closes a position the fly has not faced in that long, because the fly manages one market a pass and the book is not one market.
exposure._depthNote: THE BOUND THAT ONLY EXISTS ONCE THE ACCOUNT IS LARGE, and the one this product would otherwise have got wrong at $100k. A 25% position on $100,000 is $25,000: 4% of BTC's book within +/-0.5%, but 147% of PONS's, 2271% of ANSEM's and 5749% of CASHCAT's -- it eats the whole visible book. Size is therefore capped at this fraction of the THINNER side of the live book, because escape dumps the entire position in one order and a size you can enter but cannot leave is a trap. Read live every pass; a cap from stale depth bounds nothing. An EXIT is never capped.
exposure._deadbandNote: Applies ONLY to orders that cross. A post-only order pays no spread, so there is nothing to protect it from and blocking it would be the keeper overriding the fly for no gain.
exposure._takerNote: CROSS UNLESS CROSSING IS EXPENSIVE. Lighter charges zero maker AND zero taker fee, so the whole cost of crossing is the spread walked through, estimated per order off the live book. RAISED 6 -> 20 after three live orders in a row rested and none filled. Measured across all 57 markets: at 6bp it crosses in 41 and pays 1.4bp on average; at 20bp it crosses in 51 and pays 3.1bp. The line barely moves the cost because most books are tight -- it only binds on the few wide ones -- so the 1.7bp difference buys ten more markets it can actually get filled in. On a $5,000 slot that is about $1.55 an entry, against a resting order that does not fill costing the whole position. An EXIT ignores this and always crosses, because an exit that might not fill is not an exit.
exposure._maxTotalNote: The cap on the SUM, in notional, as a multiple of equity. slots x leverage / leverage = slots, so ten slots each allowed one equity of notional is 10x equity in aggregate. This is the number that stops the fly holding a slot in every market it has ever faced.
exposure._slotNote: TWELVE SLOTS AT 5x, so each position is about 0.4x equity and twelve of them reach the 5x aggregate cap. Smaller positions mean more of them for the same total exposure -- the same money at work, spread across more markets, and more entries to watch. It costs nothing extra: twelve positions at 0.42x equity is the same notional as ten at 0.5x.
exposure._leverageNote: FIVE, NOT TEN, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. The fly is long almost all of the time -- 88% of every decision on record -- and brain/probe-bias.js says why: driven alone, Johnston's organ puts MDN at 55.8Hz and the fly shorts, while the other five channels all drive MN9 and it goes long. With all six firing at once, five beat one. That is a property of the sense-to-drive mapping and it is NOT to be rebalanced to produce more shorts, because tuning the animal toward a trading outcome is the one thing this repo forbids. So the leverage is set around it instead. On the markets the fly actually picks -- RGTI, CLSK, ANSEM, AMC and other high-beta names -- and at their real maintenance margins: 10x is $88,000 of notional on $10,000 and is LIQUIDATED BY A 5.4% DOWN DAY. 5x is $48,000 and survives to -14.1%. 3x survives to -26.1%. Raising this back to 10 is choosing a book that a single bad session ends.
exposure._minBookNote: A MARKET WITH NO BOOK IS NOT A MARKET THIS DESK CAN OPERATE IN. Measured live: four of the 57 were showing $0 on their thin side within half a percent of mid -- RGTI at 151bp half-spread, AI at 117, WULF at 79, USO at 55. Not wide, absent. The fly turning to one costs a whole pass and yields a refusal or an order resting in a book nothing trades against. This is the DESK'S decision and not the animal's, which is why it lives in config and not in brain/: nothing about the fly changed, only which markets are put in front of it -- on the same grounds as depthFraction, since a size you can enter and cannot leave is a trap and an empty book is that trap at any size. Measured every pass, so a market that comes back to life is back in the panorama with nothing edited. Set to 0 to seat all 57 again.
exposure._minSlotFractionNote: A SLOT IS A TENTH OF THE ACCOUNT AND A MARKET THAT CANNOT TAKE ONE SHOULD NOT HOLD ONE. The depth cap stops the fly buying more than a book carries, but only AFTER the slot is spent: a market with $776 on its thin side took a $194 position, correctly sized, wasting 96% of that slot while still counting against the ten. A market must now be able to absorb at least this fraction of a slot to be seated at all. It is DERIVED from equity rather than typed -- slot = equity/slots x leverage, cap = depthFraction of the thin side -- so the bar rises with the account and thin markets drop out on their own, which is correct, because a bigger desk genuinely cannot operate in them. At 0.5 on a $10k account the universe is about 45 of 57.

execution._note: HOW ORDERS REACH THE BOOK, and the reason losses should be directional rather than executional. Lighter charges ZERO maker and ZERO taker fee, so the entire cost of trading is the spread -- and only whoever crosses it pays. Opening orders rest POST-ONLY at the touch: they fill at the price we named or not at all, which makes slippage zero by construction instead of small by assumption. The cost traded for it is adverse selection (a resting bid fills exactly when the market comes down on it), which IS directional. An ESCAPE crosses anyway -- an exit that might not fill is not an exit -- and pays half the spread once: 0.25bp on BTC, 6.8bp on PONS. Unfilled orders EXPIRE before the next pass rather than being cancelled, so nothing has to track open orders and the reconciler simply reads what actually filled.

trade._maxNotionalNote: A BUG BACKSTOP, enforced inside the signing process itself, which reads the account's equity off the exchange ITSELF rather than being told it -- that is what keeps it independent of the keeper's arithmetic. It is a MULTIPLE OF EQUITY and not a dollar figure on purpose: every other limit here scales with the account, so an absolute cap would silently start refusing every order the day the account outgrew it, and a backstop that turns into an outage is not a safety feature. At 3.0 the largest honest order -- a flip, which is 2x one slot's notional, and one slot at 10x is a whole equity of notional -- clears with room, while a sizing bug asking for ten times the account is refused. maxNotionalUsd is an OPTIONAL absolute ceiling on top; when both are set the tighter one wins. If the account cannot be read the order is refused rather than waved through.

_passNote: ms is fly time per pass and costs roughly 25x that in CPU. everySeconds is the gap between passes, which is also the market window the fly sees, because most of what it looks at has no historical endpoint.

pass._everyNote: THE BIGGEST COST DIAL, and it does NOT stay honest as the account grows. Most orders are new markets opened from zero, which no deadband touches, so the rate the fly switches markets is what drives turnover. Measured at $10,179 with an average 2.9bp to cross: 180s turns over 7x the account a day for about 0.22%/day of spread, 60s turns over 21x for 0.65%/day, 30s for 1.30%/day. SET TO 60 on 2026-09-12 -- at $10k that is roughly $66/day, which is worth paying for three times the decisions. THE CATCH IS SIZE, and it is measured too: a $50,000 order walks deeper than a $5,000 one and costs 6.9bp against 2.9bp, so the same 60s cadence on a $100k account is about 1.4%/day rather than 0.65%. RAISE THIS AS THE ACCOUNT GROWS. The percentages look scale-free because every limit is a fraction of equity; the cost per unit of notional is not.

_ponsNote: The token that funds the fly. Fees harvested from the PONS escrow become the collateral it trades. IMMUTABLE ONCE LAUNCHED -- see keeper/README.md. factory and escrow are the PONS V2 constants on Robinhood Chain 4663.

launch.name: FLYQUANT
launch.description: A complete fruit fly connectome with a wallet. 166,700 reconstructed neurons in a flight arena with 57 live perp markets; it turns toward one and its motor neurons decide the trade. Creator fees fund the account it trades with. Every position is public and every fill links to its transaction.
launch._symbolNote: name and symbol are IMMUTABLE ONCE LAUNCHED. The project is FLYQUANT; the ticker is still FLY. Change symbol here BEFORE launching if you want $FLYQUANT instead -- it cannot be edited after.
launch._launchedByNote: THE WALLET THAT SIGNS THE LAUNCH, when it is not the fee wallet. PONS indexes TokenLaunched by the LAUNCHER, so the harvester's watcher scans by this address -- but harvesting is gated on the RECIPIENT, so it then confirms the launch actually pays feeWallet.address before wiring anything in. Leave it empty and the watcher scans by the fee wallet, which is right when the same key does both.

feeWallet._note: The keeper IS the token's creatorFeeRecipient. escrow.claim() pays this address. A FRESH wallet, never one reused from another project, key via PRIVATE_KEY in the environment only.

_distributeNote: verified gates the UNATTENDED loop and only that. gasReserveEth is the operator's own float floor, which is not fee revenue and may never leave as one.

fly._note: The sink's own namespace. The core hands this back untouched and never interprets it.

deposit._note: LEG B, VERIFIED ON CHAIN BY THIS REPO rather than copied from a document. The ZkLighter deposit contract is a PROXY -- its 1,367 bytes contain no selector at all, and checking it alone would have said deposit() does not exist. The EIP-1967 implementation slot points at 0x82de5b1161c93afdfe21ba0d5343f01cd7401d90, whose 23,168 bytes DO contain 0x8a857083.
deposit.verifiedBy: eth_getCode on the proxy, EIP-1967 slot read to the implementation, selector 0x8a857083 confirmed present in its bytecode, 2026-09-12
deposit._accountOwnerNote: The L1 address that owns the Lighter account. deposit(_to=this). Set it before arming --arm-fund or the fees credit the fee wallet's own Lighter account instead.

harvest._note: Polls every checkIntervalSec and moves on two conditions. hardThresholdEth fires IMMEDIATELY -- when fees are pouring in the right cadence is now. Otherwise it harvests on the baseCadenceMin timer once there is at least softThresholdEth waiting. Below both it does nothing, because a deposit costing more gas than it moves is a loss with extra steps. Thresholds are in ETH so deciding whether to spend gas needs no price feed.
